title: Food-based iron delivery systems: A review - ScienceDirect
abstract:
Lipid-based carriers stabilized by proteins and polysaccharides enhance the mucoadhesive features to obtain a triggered release, increased iron solubility and bioavailability as well as mucosal transport. ... Iron, an essential micronutrient and a vital part of metalloproteins (hemoglobin, myoglobin, ferritin, transferrin, cytochromes, etc), acts as an essential prosthetic group for regulating, activating, and controlling of many enzymatic reactions (enzymes such as cytochrome oxidase, catalase, NADPH reductase, peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, and Fe-sulfur complex-dependent enzymes).
Dietary oligo- and poly-saccharides are interesting for delivery vehicles due to their non-toxicity, biocompatibility, and controlled release properties (Ghibaudo et al., 2018). This section draws together the central findings and future perspectives of iron-entrapped carbohydrate carriers based on the gel or ligand structure. Lipids can improve the intestinal absorption and bioavailability of entrapped molecules (both lipophilic and hydrophilic) by various mechanisms. The lipophilic nature of these delivery vectors enhances the transportation through the lipid membrane of most mammalian cells.
Lipid-based carriers stabilized by proteins and polysaccharides enhance the mucoadhesive features to obtain a triggered release, increased iron solubility and bioavailability as well as mucosal transport. ... Iron, an essential micronutrient and a vital part of metalloproteins (hemoglobin, myoglobin, ferritin, transferrin, cytochromes, etc), acts as an essential prosthetic group for regulating, activating, and controlling of many enzymatic reactions (enzymes such as cytochrome oxidase, catalase, NADPH reductase, peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, and Fe-sulfur complex-dependent enzymes).
The direct addition of iron salt in foodstuffs is so challenging due to its low solubility, bioaccessibility, and bioavailability at physiological pH. Iron bioavailability strongly depends on the presence of inhibitors or enhancers in the diet. In addition, some digestive difficulties such as diarrhea, stomachache, vomiting, or gastric mucosa damages may occur.
Our in-silico studies results showed that cur-IONPs were predicted to be potential candidates to treat IDA due to its mucoadhesive properties, which could enhance the bioavailability, time residency, and iron absorbance through GIT, in addition to its high safety profile with high drug-likeness properties and oral bioavailability.
